speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to help me understand your condition better, could you tell me when these symptoms first started and if there was any trouble during your birth? Also, have you noticed any color changes, such as turning blue, or difficulty feeding?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the prematurity and early onset, is there any history of maternal infection, chorioamnionitis, or fever during labor? Additionally, have you noticed if the newborn is grunting, flaring their nostrils, or has a "sucking chest motion" while breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas, Complete_Blood_Count, Blood_Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray. While those results are processed, does the mother have a history of diabetes or did you notice excessive fetal movement prior to birth?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the normal blood gas and CBC results; these findings help rule out sepsis and metabolic acidosis. Given the prematurity, respiratory distress starting within two hours, and physical exam signs of grunting and retractions, is there a history of maternal GBS colonization or intrapartum fever? Additionally, does the newborn require supplemental oxygen to maintain saturation above 90%?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
